takeaway: Tuberculosis damage comes mainly from the host's delayed (type IV) hypersensitivity reaction: immune pathology.

question.text: The pathogenicity of the tubercle bacillus is primarily due to which one of the following?
question.say: The pathogenicity of the tubercle bacillus is primarily due to which one of the following?

answer.text: Delayed hypersensitivity reaction against the bacteria
answer.say: The answer is a delayed hypersensitivity reaction against the bacteria.

lines.text: The tubercle bacillus hides in the lung.
lines.say: Deep in the lung hides the green tubercle bacillus.

lines.text: T cells sound the alarm: cell-mediated immunity.
lines.say: The T cells sound the alarm. Mycobacteria stimulate a specific T cell response of cell-mediated immunity.

lines.text: They build a granuloma around it.
lines.say: They build a fortress around it: a granuloma, which reduces the infection.

lines.text: The snail clock: a delayed, type IV reaction.
lines.say: The snail clock shows it is slow. This is delayed hypersensitivity, a type four reaction.

lines.text: But the T cells also damage the lung itself.
lines.say: But the same T cells pour damage onto the lung tissue itself.

lines.text: The damage comes from our own immune response: immune pathology.
lines.say: (sigh) So the damage comes mainly from the host's own immune response. This is called immune pathology.

lines.text: Remember: in TB, our own delayed hypersensitivity does the harm.
lines.say: Remember: the tubercle bacillus harms us mainly through our own delayed hypersensitivity reaction.
